CIV.note: Only 'development of digital identity' is listed; no authentication service is described.

facts.fact: ONECI's slides for ID4Africa 2026 set out an integrated CRVS-ID path in which a registered birth leads to a unique identifier and later life events, including death, update the same identity, and list supporting the digital transformation of civil registration to feed identity as an aim.
ONECI's slides for ID4Africa 2026 list under digitalisation the digitisation of civil status registers and a gradual move from paper to digital, with 692 civil registration centres in the country.

CIV.note: The deck speaks only of strengthening the legal framework of identity and access tracing; no data protection law is named.
No count or share of people enrolled in the ID system is given; the 57.6% is birth registration.
The path from birth registration to a unique identifier is shown as architecture; the deck does not say children receive the number at registration or where.
Nothing is stated about who operates, maintains or owns the ID system.
Sectors that could use the single identifier are listed as a possibility; no register is said to use it.

facts.fact: ONECI's slides for ID4Africa 2026 report 172 fixed identity enrolment centres plus mobile enrolment units and intensified enrolment campaigns, and call the unique identifier an essential structuring element.
ONECI's slides for ID4Africa 2026 list the deployment of the RNPP as an operational enabler and name consolidating an integrated national population register as a prospect.

CIV.note: Digitisation of registers is stated without saying whether local offices enter events digitally, which events, or how many offices; the 692 centres are a total only.
Social protection is listed only as a sector that could use the identifier.
Public finances are listed only as a sector that could use the identifier.
